requirement: Habeas MUST store the source dependencies selected by `finish_search` under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs` as outline inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`. Each input identifies the file, selector, and structural hash from the snapshot that supplied the selected excerpt.
rationale:
structural: The text has one structural obligation: the dependencies selected by `finish_search` must be stored as outline inputs, each identifying file, selector (`item`) and structural hash from the snapshot that supplied the excerpt. This constrains the stored form. An alternative that stored line ranges or a hash from a later workspace reopen would violate it. The supplied root `src/authoring/sdk.rs#fn[run]` implements it. For each observed `Dependency::Node` whose node is a `HabeasNode::Source` with an outline selector, `run` reopens the file through `OutlineContent::from_path` on the SDK cache. It selects the item and checks that `contents.fingerprint()` equals the observed fingerprint. A mismatch returns an error, so the hash always comes from the observing snapshot. It then builds `{"file","item","hash"}` with `structural_hash()` and passes it to `sources.record_inputs`. The other clauses describe observable behavior: which tags are selected, that earlier selections persist, and that empty or invalid calls add nothing. Those belong to the cited SDK requirement, which is context here. I did not need to follow `record_inputs` or `stored_dependencies` further, because the input shape is built in `run`.

behavioral: The subject has one behavioral obligation. The dependencies that `finish_search` selects must be stored as outline inputs, and each input must identify the file, selector and structural hash from the snapshot that supplied the excerpt. Which tags are selected, and how the original snapshot is kept, belong to the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs`. The outline-input format and validation belong to `requirements.ci.outline_inputs`. Neither needs retesting here.

Two tests cover the obligation.

1. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]` checks the harness side. It rewrites the source file after the search. It then asserts that `finish_search` returns `Dependency::Node(node, fingerprint)` carrying the fingerprint of the original snapshot. It asserts that an empty `used` list, an invalid call and unselected excerpts produce no dependencies. It asserts that reselecting a tag gives the same dependency. It also asserts that a tag from a later page gives its own dependency.

2. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[relying_on_a_helper_excerpt_makes_edits_to_that_helper_stale]` checks the end-to-end storage. It runs `author` against a mock model that searches, finishes the search with the first tag, and submits. The file is edited between the search and the finish. The test then asserts that the saved evidence `inputs` contain exactly `habeas::outline_input(project, "src/lib.rs", "fn[assert_refusal]")`, which is the file, selector and hash from the original snapshot. It asserts that the input for the explicitly read `fn[read_me]` is also present and that the unselected `fn[unselected]` is absent. It then validates the repository and asserts that an error naming `fn[assert_refusal]` and "changed" is reported. That shows the stored hash is the original one and that the stored input is a working outline input.

Together these cover storage as outline inputs, the file/selector/hash content, use of the original snapshot rather than the edited file, and exclusion of unselected excerpts. I found no unexercised obligation or boundary in the subject text. Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.

text: :::{req} finish_search.inputs

Habeas MUST store the source dependencies selected by `finish_search` under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs` as outline inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`. Each input identifies the file, selector, and structural hash from the snapshot that supplied the selected excerpt.
:::{req} finish_search.inputs
For each selected tag, the harness records the node identity and fingerprint
from the snapshot that produced the delivered excerpt. If the excerpt also shows source owned by other outline nodes, record those nodes’ read fingerprints as well. Selecting a tag again
preserves the original dependency. Earlier selections survive later calls.
An empty `used` list adds no dependency. Unselected excerpts and the match set
add none either. An invalid call leaves all recorded inputs intact.
:::{req} outline_inputs
For an outline input, Habeas MUST parse `file` with its language's grammar under
{cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and resolve `item` to exactly one
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. It MUST
compare `hash` with the node's current structural hash under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. For display and reference coverage, it MUST derive the inclusive line range
from the first and last bytes of the SDK outline item's attachment-inclusive
span under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.item_span`. An empty
span covers the line at its start. Moving the node, editing other
nodes, or editing comments its profile does not hash MUST NOT invalidate the
input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, parse failure,
invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed hash.
:::{example} search_accounting.helper_freshness
A marked test calls `assert_refusal`. A search excerpt of that helper supplies
the refusal and byte-preservation assertions used to justify the judgment.
The model finishes the search with the helper's tag without reading it with
`read_node`. Saved evidence MUST include the helper's outline input.
Replacing the helper with a no-op MUST make that evidence stale, even when
the marked test source is unchanged.
